def two_stage_makespan(jobs):
    """Compute the minimum total completion time for a two-stage workshop.

    A workshop has one washing machine and one drying machine. There are
    n items (0 <= n <= 200); item i is described by jobs[i] = (w, d)
    with integers 1 <= w, d <= 10**9: the item needs w seconds of
    washing followed by d seconds of drying. Each machine handles one
    item at a time and runs each job without interruption. An item may
    start drying only after its own washing has finished and the dryer
    is free.

    You choose a single processing order (one permutation of the items).
    The washer processes the items back-to-back in that order starting
    at time 0, and the dryer processes them in the same order, each
    item as early as possible. Return the minimum possible time, over
    all n! orders, at which the last item finishes drying, as an exact
    integer. Return 0 for an empty list. The answer is a single integer,
    so no tie-breaking among equally good orders is needed.

    Bounds: n <= 200, so a correct solution must run essentially
    instantly; enumerating all orders is impossible, and simple
    orderings (by washing time, by drying time, by total time, etc.)
    are not optimal in general.

    >>> two_stage_makespan([(3, 2), (1, 4)])
    7
    >>> two_stage_makespan([(5, 1), (1, 5), (3, 3)])
    10
    >>> two_stage_makespan([])
    0
    """
